note: Made-up personas for the demo. Each one mixes patterns from several interviews and doesn't stand for any one person.

personas.name: Maya
personas.about: AI-forward but not technical, and a regular at OCS. She uses ChatGPT's free plan for almost everything and only wants free tools.
personas.shows: A gap at the right moment, the one-card-a-day limit, and coaching on a tool she already has.

steps.title: Coffee chat w/ Yale alum at Bain
steps.narration: Maya has no notetaker and the chat starts in 15 minutes. This is the gap the app is for. Point out the consent note, then click Set it up.

steps.title: ECON group project sync
steps.narration: Same kind of moment, but Maya has Granola now, so it stays quiet. If she skipped setup, it would have coached her on Zoom's summary instead, and held it for tomorrow.

scene.title: ChatGPT
scene.detail: Explain price elasticity like I'm prepping for a case interview.

steps.title: ECON group presentation
steps.narration: Slides are a real gap, but Maya already had today's card. It waits in the menu bar instead of interrupting. Open the menu bar to show it waiting.

scene.title: ChatGPT
scene.detail: Explain price elasticity like I'm prepping for a case interview.

steps.title: OCS mock interview
steps.narration: The evening before an interview is a calm moment. Maya already has ChatGPT, so it coaches her on voice mode instead of selling her a new app. It's still over today's limit, so this waits too and replaces the slides card.
New day. The waiting card shows up at the first calm moment. Click Show me how for the one-minute rundown.

personas.name: Theo
personas.tagline: Architecture sophomore who lives in Claude
personas.about: Pays for Claude and does most of his thinking there. Uses Figma every day. Won't install another app unless it's clearly worth it, and he turned the daily limit up to three.
personas.shows: Coaching on tools inside Claude, like a connector and Claude Slides, before anything new, and Not for me sticking.

steps.title: Figma
steps.narration: Going back and forth between Claude and Figma counts as a design moment. Claude is his main app, and Figma's connector for Claude lets it read a frame from a link, so it coaches that instead of selling him something. Click Show me how.

scene.title: Claude
scene.detail: Give me three massing options for a library on a corner lot.

steps.title: ARCH 2810 seminar readings
steps.narration: Claude Projects ranks first because Claude is Theo's main app. It's a feature he already pays for.

steps.title: Studio review presentation
steps.narration: Keynote has no AI drafting, but Claude can build a deck he can open in Keynote, so it coaches Claude Slides before suggesting a new app. Theo would rather lay out his own boards. Click Not for me.

steps.title: Final review presentation practice
steps.narration: Another presentation. Theo said slide tools aren't for him, so it stays quiet. That choice sticks.

personas.name: Ines
personas.tagline: Sociology senior who's careful about privacy
personas.about: Likes doing her own notes and her own writing. Uses Perplexity and Gemini Notebook in the browser. During onboarding she turned off notetakers and writing help.
personas.shows: Staying quiet is the point. A careful user gets one card all day.

steps.title: Office hours with Prof. Alvarez
steps.narration: Quiet. Ines turned off notetakers, and it respects that every time.

steps.title: SOCY 3410 seminar readings
steps.narration: Quiet. She told us she already uses Gemini Notebook for readings.

steps.title: Thesis chapter due to advisor
steps.narration: Quiet. Writing help is switched off.

steps.title: Dinner w/ roommates
steps.narration: Quiet. Apple's model reads this as personal, right on the Mac.

steps.title: Fellowship interview
steps.narration: Her only card all day: Big Interview, which OCS gives students for free. One useful card beats five ignored ones.

personas.name: Dev
personas.tagline: Cognitive Science junior who collects tools
personas.about: Installs every tool he hears about, then forgets them. Grammarly, Cursor and Notion haven't been opened in two months. Uses Gemini most, and set the daily limit to three.
personas.shows: For someone who already has tools, the app is a coach, not a store.

steps.title: Jane Street cover letter due
steps.narration: Dev already has Grammarly and hasn't opened it in two months. It coaches him on what he owns before suggesting anything new.

steps.title: Visual Studio Code
steps.narration: A coding moment. Cursor is on his Mac but unused, so this is another coaching card, not another install. Click Show me how.

steps.title: PSYC 2300 midterm
steps.narration: Gemini is Dev's main app, so Guided Learning ranks first among the study tools he already has.

scene.title: Gemini
scene.detail: Summarize the key theories for PSYC 2300.

scene.title: Lecture notes
scene.detail: article:PSYC 2300: Memory and attention, lecture notes

personas.name: Grace
personas.tagline: First-year who's curious but has nothing set up
personas.about: Interested in AI and in recruiting, but no main AI app yet. Her day is packed.
personas.shows: Lots of gaps doesn't mean lots of pop-ups. Nothing interrupts a call.

steps.title: Study group on Zoom
steps.narration: Grace joins a Zoom call. While she's on a call, nothing pops up.

steps.title: Coffee chat with Lisa, Class of '22
steps.narration: A real gap, but she's mid-call, so the card waits.
The call ends and the waiting card shows up straight away, ten minutes before the coffee chat.

steps.title: Goldman Sachs info session
steps.narration: Covered now if she set up Granola. Otherwise she's had today's card and this waits.

steps.title: BIOL 1010 midterm
steps.narration: Study tools are a gap too, but one card a day is the limit. This waits.

steps.title: Writing seminar essay due
steps.narration: Another gap, another wait. Several gaps today, and Grace saw one card.

personas.name: Rory
personas.tagline: Political Science junior recruiting for consulting
personas.about: Pays for ChatGPT Plus and uses it for everything, mostly by pasting things back and forth. Turned on window titles and screen looks during onboarding, and picked consulting and policy as career goals.
personas.shows: What the coach learns from how you work: tips and ready-made prompts for the app you already have, a never-read list, and cards that wait while you're writing. No new apps all day.

steps.narration: Rory keeps pasting paragraphs between ChatGPT and Word. The coach looks at the letter on the Mac and keeps one line about it. It has a tip, but Rory has put off cards in Word before, so it waits. Open the menu to show what it learned.

scene.detail: Can you make this sound more confident? "At the nonprofit I helped analyze eviction filings across four neighborhoods."

steps.narration: Rory leaves Word for ChatGPT, so the waiting tip shows up. It's a workflow for the app Rory already pays for, and the prompt already says McKinsey. Click Show me, then Copy prompt.

scene.detail: Can you make this sound more confident? "At the nonprofit I helped analyze eviction filings across four neighborhoods."

steps.narration: Rory is reading an alum's profile, and the calendar has a McKinsey coffee chat at noon. Rory picked consulting as a career goal, so the prompt asks consulting questions. No new app, just a better way to use ChatGPT.

scene.detail: profile:Alex Chen|Engagement Manager at McKinsey & Company|Washington, DC|linkedin.com/in/alexchen-yale

steps.title: Coffee chat w/ Yale alum at McKinsey
steps.narration: The coffee chat itself is covered. Rory already uses Granola, so there's no card.

scene.detail: profile:Alex Chen|Engagement Manager at McKinsey & Company|Washington, DC|linkedin.com/in/alexchen-yale

steps.narration: Rory opens Passwords. It's on the never-read list, so the coach doesn't take a picture at all, and nothing pops up while it's open.

Now Rory is reading the McKinsey posting. The coach remembers the letter from this morning, by its label only, and offers a check of the letter against the posting. That's the third card today, and still no new app.

scene.detail: posting:McKinsey & Company|Business Analyst Intern, Summer 2027|Washington, DC and other offices|mckinsey.com/careers
